nodes.description: Bilateral absence of breasts and nipples in the single woman with a PTPRF-disrupting balanced translocation. Her other features (ectodermal dysplasia with absent upper incisors and brittle nails, small cup-shaped pinnae, and unilateral renal agenesis) have not been seen in the homozygous family and are not attributed to BNAH2 here.

nodes.description: A homozygous frameshift variant truncates PTPRF (LAR), a receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase with an adhesion-molecule-like extracellular region and two cytoplasmic phosphatase domains. Loss of the phosphatase is presumed to remove LAR-dependent tyrosine dephosphorylation at epithelial junctions. In the translocation case, one allele was disrupted and PTPRF RNA and protein were severely reduced in lymphoblastoid cells, which is consistent with near-complete loss of function, though the second hit was not identified.

Whether breast tissue itself is absent in biallelic carriers is not reported, as the affected individuals were children. In the translocation case, both breasts and nipples were absent.

nodes.description: LAR localizes to adherens junctions, associates with cadherin complexes and dephosphorylates beta-catenin, and also localizes to focal adhesions. It has been proposed that loss of this activity in the developing nipple-areola epithelium perturbs cell-cell contact, peptide growth factor signaling or canonical Wnt signaling. This node records that hypothesis; which, if any, of these routes operates in nipple development has not been tested.

nodes.description: Mice lacking the sequences encoding both LAR phosphatase domains develop normally, but homozygous females cannot deliver milk because alveoli fail to complete terminal differentiation in late pregnancy. The model shows a mammary-gland requirement for LAR but does not report a nipple or areola defect, so it does not recapitulate the human nipple-areola phenotype.
